## About this site

This guide covers the parts of UK Biobank analysis that begin where
[ukbAid](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/ukbAid/) ends: how to extract,
clean, and work with clinical records — GP diagnoses, hospital episodes, and
medication prescriptions — once your project is set up and running on the
Research Analysis Platform (RAP).

It is written for collaborators and students at Steno Diabetes Center Aarhus
who are new to the UK Biobank platform or new to working with linked clinical
data.

---

## Before you start

::: {.callout-important}
### Start with ukbAid

Before reading anything on this site, complete the
[ukbAid setup](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/ukbAid/articles/initial-setup.html).
This covers requesting RAP access, creating your GitHub account and personal
access token, installing the ukbAid package, and cloning your project
repository. None of the scripts on this site will work without that
foundation in place.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Install ukbrapR every session

The RAP environment resets when a session ends — packages do not persist.
At the start of every RAP RStudio session, install and load ukbrapR:

```r
pak::pak("lcpilling/ukbrapR")
library(ukbrapR)
```

ukbrapR is used throughout this guide for GP clinical record extraction,
Hospital Episode Statistics queries, and data management. The full session
startup sequence is in [scripts/setup.R](../scripts/setup.R).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### `ukbrapR` documentation: run `export_tables()` once before GP or HES extraction

According to the [`ukbrapR` README on GitHub](https://github.com/lcpilling/ukbrapR/blob/main/README.md),
`get_diagnoses()` requires the linked tables to be exported to RAP persistent
storage first — once per project:

```r
ukbrapR::export_tables()
```

This takes several minutes and exports approximately 10 GB. You never need
to repeat it. See [Getting Started](getting-started-ukb.qmd) for details.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Note for discussion

UKDC's extraction scripts call `get_diagnoses()` without first running
`export_tables()` and return diagnoses correctly. Whether this step is truly
required or is already handled upstream is unclear. **To clarify with
supervisors.**
:::

## Folder structure

When this project is set up as a standalone repository, the layout is:

```
ukb-clinical-guide/        <- project root (future GitHub repository)
├── scripts/
│   ├── setup.R            <- session startup: packages, demographics, save pattern
│   ├── extract_diagnoses.R   <- GP + HES extraction using a code list CSV
│   └── extract_medications.R    <- prescription extraction: BNF and regex approaches
├── docs/
│   ├── _quarto.yml        <- site configuration (theme, navbar, footer)
│   ├── index.qmd          <- this page
│   ├── getting-started-ukb.qmd
│   ├── code-lists-guide.qmd
│   ├── guide-to-functions.qmd
│   ├── dataset-reference.qmd
│   └── common-mistakes.qmd
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── publish.yml    <- GitHub Actions: render site and deploy to GitHub Pages
```
